summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, anxiety, and recurrent abdominal pain was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain lasting three days. She had been unable to eat or take medications, leading to hyperglycemia and acute kidney injury with creatinine rising to 1.6. In the ED, she was agitated with hypertensive urgency, managed with Ativan and Haldol. IV fluids, insulin, antiemetics, and pain control were initiated. Her symptoms improved, she tolerated oral intake, and labs showed resolution of kidney injury and downtrending white count. Asymptomatic bacteriuria was noted but not treated. Lisinopril was held due to recent kidney injury. She was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her PCP for medication management and a dermatology referral for breast lesions.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic (poly)neuropathy
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
